Visit note | 2025-09-27 04:00 PM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Shahana Pramanik, 59, female. Mrs. Pramanik returns for review, reporting that she gets breathless on the stairs, her nails are brittle, and she feels constantly tired. She states these symptoms started after a stomach illness during a stay in Motijheel. She works as a hotel receptionist and has no known comorbidities. On examination, haemoglobin 10.3 g/dL, BP 116/78 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, and weight 78 kg. Heart and lung sounds are clear. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

She mentions that her complaints began during a hot week with little water intake in Bogura. She works as a textile engineer and has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination, temperature 100.0°F, BP 112/80 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, and weight 74 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild suprapubic tenderness. Assessment: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least two litres of water daily and not to hold urine for long periods. Follow-up in 1 week if symptoms continue.
